idea-plugin.name: SQL Dialect for DuckDB (embedded & Quack)
idea-plugin.description:
A real DuckDB SQL dialect for DataGrip and IntelliJ-family IDEs, with ready-to-use data sources for local/embedded DuckDB and GizmoSQL servers (Arrow-free quack-jdbc driver).

  • Built-in PIPE authoring: enable DuckDB PIPE under Settings > Tools, write FROM t |> WHERE ... |> SELECT ..., and execute as DuckDB SQL. Includes generated-SQL preview and run-to-stage. No SQL Transpiler plugin required; ordinary FROM-first queries are unchanged.
  • DuckDB syntax, measured: correct statement and run-block boundaries across the DuckDB statement surface — SELECT * EXCLUDE(...), QUALIFY, GROUP BY ALL, struct/list literals, lambdas, PIVOT/UNPIVOT, FROM-first queries, ATTACH, SUMMARIZE, CREATE MACRO/SECRET. Coverage is scored against DuckDB's own test suite: 226/226 sampled syntax families at DuckDB 1.5.5.
  • Engine-exact error checking: statements are validated by a real DuckDB (from your data source's driver; parse-only, never binds or executes) — squiggles carry the engine's own messages, so there is zero grammar drift.
  • Completion that follows your engine: on connect the catalog is harvested live from duckdb_functions() — your engine version, your loaded extensions. Run INSTALL/LOAD and completion updates itself; autoloaded extensions arrive via Refresh DuckDB Catalog (editor right-click). Offline you get bundled version-aware metadata, plus "requires <extension>" hints for extension functions.
  • Two data sources, one dialect: local file / in-memory DuckDB, and GizmoSQL over jdbc:quack:// (default port 9494). Driver versions are pinned and auto-download from Maven Central, matched to the tested engine.

GizmoSQL connection notes: paste your token into the Password field (stored in the IDE's secure storage) and leave User blank; TLS is off by default — add tls=true in the URL parameters for HTTPS endpoints.

Known issue: cancelling a running query over a GizmoSQL connection is currently a no-op in the quack driver — the query keeps running server-side. Local/embedded cancel works. A driver fix is tracked.

This is an independent, community plugin developed by Sortdev SRL, not affiliated with DuckDB Labs, the DuckDB Foundation, or GizmoSQL. "DuckDB" is a trademark of the DuckDB Foundation, used only to identify the database this plugin supports. DuckDB logo used per the DuckDB design manual.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
0.3.5 - dogfood build with formal Brikk releases and shared column completion.
  • Uses brikk-sql 0.19.1, SQL IntelliJ support 0.1.1 and Kotlin IntelliJ support 0.2.0 from Maven Central.
  • Shows brikk column types, nullability and source aliases using the shared renderer.
  • Keeps same-named join columns distinct without changing insertion text or SQL scope selection.
  • No Maven Local dependency or native database engine is bundled.
0.3.4 - shared SQL support backport.
  • Source builds now use formal brikk-sql 0.19.1 and Brikk Kotlin IntelliJ support 0.2.0.
  • Brikk SQL IntelliJ support 0.1.1 provides shared column presentation, including distinct suggestions for join aliases.
  • Maven Local and the temporary lexical guard are removed.
  • Earlier local testing ZIPs used brikk-sql 0.19.0-SNAPSHOT to validate the upstream unfinished-comment fix.
  • No native engine, verification library or compiler plugin is bundled.
0.3.3 - shared SQL IntelliJ support backport.
  • Uses Brikk SQL IntelliJ support 0.1.0 for cooperative Execute actions and translated scripts.
  • Uses brikk-sql 0.19.0 for statement boundaries and parser-backed parameter discovery.
  • Substitutes parameters before lowering, rejects stale preparation and keeps DuckDB validation policy.
0.3.2 - shared Brikk relation-contract support.
  • Uses the published Brikk Kotlin IntelliJ support 0.1.0 library from Maven Central.
  • Resolves, completes and navigates Kotlin relation-input columns with statement-local aliases, joins and stage scopes supported by DuckDB PIPE syntax.
  • Preserves partial/unavailable contract distinctions and labelled generated-column navigation fallbacks. Kotlin remains optional.
0.3.1 - automatic DuckDB Brikk editing in Kotlin K2.
  • Recognizes resolved Sql.duckdb calls inside @BrikkSql and enables PIPE editing for that host without changing project settings.
  • Scalar Kotlin interpolations become named SQL binds while preserving Kotlin references and rename. Relation slots and literal constants retain their roles.
  • Preserves trimmed/escaped source mappings and rejects unsupported interpolations. Kotlin is optional; ordinary SQL and Doris injections are unchanged.
0.3.0 - built-in, per-project PIPE support.
  • Bundles brikk-sql 0.18.0 for PIPE translation, with no native database engine.
  • Enable under Settings > Tools > DuckDB PIPE. Defaults off.
  • Preview generated SQL, run stages up to the caret, and execute mixed scripts with normal console parameter prompting. Unsafe translations are blocked.
  • Cooperative Execute wrappers preserve Doris and other dialect handlers.
0.2.0 — the injected-SQL language id is now DuckDBSQL (was DuckDBBrikk), so embedding DuckDB SQL in a host language (Kotlin/Java string injection, @Language) reads cleanly. If you had manually set a file's dialect, re-pick DuckDB (sort.dev) once; connected data sources are unaffected.
0.1.1 — polish.
  • Fixed the DuckDB icon rendering oversized in the data source / driver UI.
  • Clearer names: the dialect is DuckDB (sort.dev), and the data-source drivers are DuckDB Embedded (sort.dev) and DuckDB via Quack (sort.dev) — distinct from the stock generic DuckDB driver.
  • Refreshed README; Kotlin/build toolchain updated. No behavior changes.

0.1.0 — first public release.
  • DuckDB dialect with correct statement/run-block boundaries — coverage measured against DuckDB's own test suite (226/226 sampled syntax families at DuckDB 1.5.5).
  • Engine-exact error checking by a real DuckDB from your driver (EXPLAIN-based, never executes).
  • Live per-connection completion: functions/keywords harvested from the connected engine (version- and extension-exact), refreshed automatically when INSTALL/LOAD runs in a console, or on demand via Refresh DuckDB Catalog; bundled 943-function snapshot offline, with "requires <extension>" hints.
  • Object tree from DuckDB's JDBC metadata — ATTACHed databases appear as catalogs, on both drivers.
  • Ready-made data sources: local/embedded DuckDB and GizmoSQL (token-auth quack-jdbc, port 9494); pinned drivers auto-download from Maven Central.
  • Known issue: query cancel over GizmoSQL is a quack-driver no-op (local cancel works); driver fix tracked.

action.description: Re-read functions, keywords, and loaded extensions from the connected DuckDB engine
